subject.title: fix(ui): apply Context Profile presets via config.patch to avoid SecretRef rejection

question: After rebasing onto current main, should Context Profile application permanently use the narrow `config.patch` contract while preserving dirty form/raw drafts and adopting the post-write configuration hash?
rationale: The implementation is technically plausible, but config loading, optimistic concurrency, and persisted draft behavior are compatibility-sensitive owner boundaries whose permanent contract should be confirmed against current main before merge.

options.title: Land the narrow patch contract
options.body: Rebase, retain the three-field `config.patch` path and reconciliation tests, then require exact-head UI and SecretRef proof before merge.

options.title: Rework through full-form submission
options.body: Keep presets staged in the shared full-config Save/Apply flow and repair that workflow instead, accepting a broader SecretRef and form-serialization change.

options.title: Pause the preset workflow
options.body: Remove or disable Context Profiles until maintainers choose a unified configuration-write model, leaving the linked P1 workflow unavailable.

recommendation.title: Land the narrow patch contract
recommendation.body: Rebase, retain the three-field `config.patch` path and reconciliation tests, then require exact-head UI and SecretRef proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision depends most directly on the SecretRef restoration and config-write contract established by their prior merged work.
